newsitem.title: USA: Stocks boosted by Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Stocks boosted by Greenspan comments.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks powered higher Friday on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's latest comments, which implied that the central bank was not likely to raise interest rates later this month.
Shortly after 10 a.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 50.57 points at 7,187.19. In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines by 4-1 margin.
In a speech late Thursday to New York University's Stern School of Business, Greenspan said that he expected the nation's economic growth to decelerate later this year and into next year.
The comments were interpreted by some to mean that the Fed would not raise rates at the next meeting of the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee on May 20.
But even if it were to raise rates, a further tightening by 25 basis points may already have been discounted by the market.
Bonds also shot higher, with the Treasury's benchmark 30-year bond up 22/32, lowering its yield to 6.88 percent from 6.94 percent on Thursday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The central bank on March 25 raised short-term interest rates for the first time in more than two years in an effort to keep the economy from overheating and thus sustain the expansion.
Wall Street has been on pins and needles since then, expecting the Fed to raise interest rates again.
Greenspan spent much of his speech defending the Fed's quarter percentage point rate increase on March 25 against what he called "more than the usual share of ... criticism."
"The Federal Open Market Committee raised rates as a form of insurance," Greenspan said. "It was a small, prudent step."
The stock market was also following through on Thursday's advance in reaction to news of a proposal to make a capital gains tax cut effective as of Wednesday.
After the stock market closed Wednesday, the Republican chairmen of the congressional tax-writing committees said they would propose setting May 7 as the effective date for a capital gains tax.
The tax cut would allow investors to keep more of their profits when they sell stocks.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 9.74 points at 1,340.57.
